title: CRISPR-dCas9 System for Targeting Promoter Regions in HEK293 Cells
author: Alkhayer, Ponath, et al.

steps.title: Phosphorylate and anneal gRNA oligos
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µL master mix with 1 µL forward oligo (100 µM), 1 µL reverse oligo (100 µM), 1 µL 10× Ligation Buffer, 0.5 µL T4 PNK and nuclease‑free water to 10 µL; incubate 37 °C 30 min, heat‑inactivate 95 °C 5 min, cool to 25 °C, then dilute the annealed oligos 1:250 in nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Culture and transfect HEK293 cells
steps.instruction: Thaw HEK293 cells and grow in DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen/strep at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂; passage 2–5 times weekly and use cells at passage 2–5. Seed 5–6 × 10⁶ cells in a 15 cm dish with 20 mL DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen/strep 20 h before transfection. Replace medium 3 h before transfection with pen/strep‑free DMEM + 10 % FBS. Prepare transfection mix: tube A – 40 µL Lipofectamine 2000 diluted in 750 µL serum‑free Opti‑MEM; tube B – 750 µL Opti‑MEM + 16 µg DNA (8 µg dCas9‑puro vector + 8 µg gRNA‑MICA‑T1 vector). Vortex, incubate 5 min at 20‑22 °C, add tube A to tube B, mix, incubate 20 min at 20‑22 °C. Add mixture dropwise to the dish in a circular motion, incubate 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ ~17 h. Replace transfection medium next day with DMEM + 10 % FBS + 1 % pen/strep. Assess transfection efficiency with pEGFP‑C1 plasmid by fluorescence microscopy. After 48 h, proceed to enChIP.

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate chromatin with antibodies
steps.instruction: Collect 1 % of the soluble chromatin volume (3 µL) as input and store at 4 °C. To the remaining chromatin (~20 mL), add 4 µg IgG antibody to 300 µL for the control IP and 100–120 µg Cas9 antibody to the rest for the experimental IP. Incubate 16 h at 4 °C on a roller. Transfer 300 µL of the Cas9‑IP to a new tube for qPCR; keep the remainder for mass‑spectrometry. Add 50 µL A+G blocked‑beads slurry to each IP, gently invert to mix, and rotate 1 h at 4 °C (mix bead slurry by gentle inversion before pipetting; cut the tip off a 200 µL pipette tip to aid removal).

steps.title: Set up qPCR for target detection
steps.instruction: For each of the three samples (input, Cas9‑IP, IgG‑IP) assemble a 10 µL qPCR master mix: 1 µL DNA, 5 µL SYBR‑Green Mix, 0.25 µL 10 µM forward primer (ChIP‑qPCR MICA_fw), 0.25 µL 10 µM reverse primer (ChIP‑qPCR MICA_rev), 3.5 µL H₂O. Run the following cycling program: 95 °C 15 min (initial denaturation); 95 °C 20 s (denaturation); 60 °C 15 s (annealing); 72 °C 60 s (extension); repeat for 40 cycles; 72 °C 5 min (final extension); hold at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash immunoprecipitation beads
steps.instruction: Keep all samples on ice. Centrifuge each IP at 300 × g for 1 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Add 1 mL cold Wash Buffer I, invert gently, centrifuge 300 × g 1 min 4 °C, discard. Wash with 1 mL Wash Buffer II, invert, centrifuge 300 × g 1 min 4 °C, discard. Wash with 1 mL Wash Buffer III, centrifuge 300 × g 1 min 4 °C, discard. Repeat the Wash Buffer III step once more. Add 1 mL elution buffer (EB, QIAGEN), mix gently, centrifuge 300 × g 1 min at 20‑22 °C, discard supernatant; repeat the elution‑buffer step. Beads may be washed with a vacuum system (QIAvac 24 Plus) if desired.

steps.title: Elute DNA and proteins from beads
steps.instruction: Prepare 400 µL fresh elution buffer per sample (including input). Incubate beads with 200 µL elution buffer 15 min at 20‑22 °C while shaking at 1,200 rpm. Centrifuge 17,000 × g 2 min at 20‑22 °C, transfer supernatant to a new tube. Repeat the incubation and centrifugation, then combine the two supernatants. Add 400 µL elution buffer to each input sample. Add 42 µL freshly prepared Reversion Mix Buffer to every sample, vortex, and incubate 16 h at 65 °C (samples may be stored at 4 °C and DNA purified within two days).

steps.title: Purify DNA using spin columns
steps.instruction: Mix each eluate with 2.2 mL Binding Buffer PB in a 5 mL tube, apply to a QIAquick Spin Column, and centrifuge 17,000 × g 1 min at 20‑22 °C; discard flow‑through. Add 1 mL PE Buffer, centrifuge 17,000 × g 1 min at 20‑22 °C. Transfer the column to a new tube, add 30 µL elution buffer, incubate 2 min at 20‑22 °C, then centrifuge at high speed 2 min at 20‑22 °C. The purified DNA (1 µL per reaction) is ready for qPCR.

steps.title: Quantify DNA by qPCR
steps.instruction: Set up the same 10 µL qPCR master mix as in step 4 for each purified DNA sample. Use the following cycling program: 95 °C 15 min (initial denaturation); 95 °C 15 s (denaturation); 60 °C 20 s (annealing); 72 °C 15 s (extension); repeat for 40 cycles; 95 °C 60 s; 72 °C 30 s; melt curve 72‑95 °C increasing 0.5 °C per 10 s step. Calculate enrichment of the target locus as Input % = 2^{-(C_T sample − C_T input)} (input represents 1 % of soluble chromatin).

steps.title: Prepare Cas9‑IP for mass spectrometry
steps.instruction: Add 1.5 mL A+G blocked beads to the Cas9‑IP sample, incubate 1 h at 4 °C on a roller. Centrifuge 1,200 × g 2 min at 4 °C, aspirate supernatant. Wash beads sequentially with 20 mL Wash Buffer I, 20 mL Wash Buffer II, and twice with 20 mL Wash Buffer III, inverting gently each time and centrifuging 1,200 × g 2 min at 4 °C after each wash (keep samples on ice and handle beads carefully; a vacuum system may be used). Wash twice with 20 mL EB buffer, centrifuge 1,200 × g 2 min at 4 °C, aspirate. Store beads at –80 °C in 200 µL EB buffer containing 1× protease‑inhibitor cocktail. Perform off‑bead digestion using 6 M urea / 2 M thiourea with 10 mM DTT, followed by high‑pH reversed‑phase separation and LC‑MS² label‑free quantitation.

description: The analysis of the transcription factors responsible for the expression of a specific gene remains technically challenging as they are only present in low abundance at the site of interest.2,3,4 Recently we identified potential transcription factors associated with the promoter of the NK cell activating ligand MICA1 based on a previously described technique referred to as in situ capture of chromatin utilizing an inactive Cas9 (dCas9).5 In combination with a guide RNA (gRNA) targeting the promoter region of MICA, we applied this method to retain dCas9 at the site of interest, followed by Cas9 antibody-mediated pull-down and subsequent analysis of bound proteins and DNA by mass spectrometry and PCR, respectively.
